subject: Model fit intake & sensitive query harvest — DeepMed AI
messages:
From: Sophie Zhang <sophie.zhang@deepmed.ai>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + call recap (DeepMed AI / Redwood)

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the demo today. I pulled together a quick recap for my team and a first pass at the types of queries we expect our assistant to handle. Attached is a CSV with ~120 sample prompts (mix of clinical triage, product data lookup, and patient-data summarization examples).

A few clarifications from our side:
- Many prompts include PHI-like tokens (patient initials, MRN fragments). We need recommendations on what to redact vs what to pseudo-tag for downstream context.
- Latency requirement: 95th pct under 600ms for short queries (<=50 tokens).
- Cost sensitivity: we want a model under $0.0009/token average for our burst profile.
- Safety: anything that generates clinical recommendations must trigger a citation + liability-safe fallback.

We also had a question about whether you can run evals on our provided prompt set and return model-level pass/fail for hallucination thresholds.

Attaching the CSV now: deepmed-prompt-samples.csv (CSV).

Best —
Sophie
Head of Product, DeepMed AI

From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Zhang <sophie.zhang@deepmed.ai>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + call recap (DeepMed AI / Redwood)

Hi Sophie — great to meet earlier, and thanks for sending the prompt set. I uploaded the CSV to our intake Drive folder and looped in Marcus and Vanessa to accelerate the evaluation plan.

Quick answers up front:
- We can run an internal eval suite across 3 candidate families we discussed: RW-3B-instruct (fast, low-cost), RW-7B-chat-q4 (balanced quality with quantized weights), and RW-13B-chat (higher-quality, higher-cost).
- We’ll produce a small benchmark report with per-model: latency p50/p95, token-cost estimate, and three hallucination metrics (fact-consistency, citation-needed rate, and boundary-failure rate) mapped to your safety thresholds.
- For PHI guidance: we recommend redaction for direct identifiers (MRN, SSNs) and pseudo-tagging for contextual tokens (e.g., PATIENT_NAME -> [PATIENT]). We’ll include an abridged redaction playbook (first draft attached).

Next steps proposed:
1) Redwood runs the eval on your CSV + a 50-edgecase set we’ll sketch (turnaround 3 business days).
2) We share the benchmark dashboard and a short recomendation memo with model + quantization picks.
3) If you approve, we’ll schedule a 60-min run-through with engineering to validate integration points and data flows.

Can you confirm the benchmark scope (only the CSV, or shall we include a small synthetic PHI-heavy set)? Also, do you want us to evaluate streaming vs non-streaming latency?

Thanks —
Sofia
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: sofie-team@deepmed.ai <sophie.zhang@deepmed.ai>
Cc: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:51:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + call recap (DeepMed AI / Redwood)

Sophie — quick follow-up from our internal triage after reviewing the CSV: thanks for the rich set. A few items Marcus and I flagged that will shape model recommendations and redaction rules: 

- Edgecase cluster A: many short imperative prompts asking for differential diagnoses without patient vitals. Those are high risk for hallucination; we’ll mark them as "require-citation-or-fallback."
- Edgecase cluster B: multi-turn context where identity tokens are interleaved; we should pseudonymize tokens before model input to keep cache reuse benefits.
- Aggregation prompts that ask for longitudinal summaries (multi-document): these need larger context windows; RW-13B-chat or a tiled-inference approach will perform better.

Preliminary model fit advice (internal):
- If cost is the primary constraint, start with RW-3B-instruct quantized + prefix-cache (expect lower latency, watch hallucination).
- For a mix of cost & safety, RW-7B-chat-q4 + conservative decoding and a citation overlay (automated retrieval that must match before answer) is our recommended baseline.
- Reserve RW-13B-chat for flagged workflows (clinical summaries, discharge notes).

Attachments I’m sending: redaction-guidelines-draft.md (contains regex suggestions and a fast pseudo-tag mapping), and a small edgecase sketch (50 examples) that we will use to stress-test hallucination.

Operational asks for DeepMed to confirm:
- Which PHI token types you want redacted vs pseudonymized (we included a checklist in the draft).
- Whether we can seed the eval with a synthetic PHI-heavy set (we will generate, but need sign-off).

If you approve, we’ll run the first eval slice tomorrow and post results to the benchmark link (https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/deepmed-2027).

—Vanessa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Zhang <sophie.zhang@deepmed.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + call recap (DeepMed AI / Redwood)

Thanks all — this looks great. Quick answers:
- Approve including the synthetic PHI-heavy set (please flag it clearly in reports).
- Redact direct identifiers (SSN, MRN) and pseudonymize names and dates — see the two-column checklist in the CSV (column REDACT_HINT).
- We’d like both streaming and non-streaming latency profiled if possible.

Next steps for us: we’ll review the redaction draft and return any legal comments by EOD Friday. Expect a legal contact (legal@deepmed.ai) to join the thread shortly for SOC/contract-level asks.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Sophie
Head of Product, DeepMed AI
